assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic and satiety effects) led to a therapeutic class that has transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care and shows cardiovascular and renal benefit. The chain from physiology to drug is unusually clear, original and of very large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 biology in humans, secretion and action) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, DPP-4 degradation, translation) are central to the physiology; Knudsen led development of the long-acting liraglutide/semaglutide analogues. Mojsov's contribution to identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is part of the historical credit, and credit among Mojsov, Habener and others is contested; I choose three from the supplied names but this is a genuine allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Multiple large, independent randomized outcome trials and years of real-world use confirm efficacy and safety; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely given the field's current prominence.
uncertainties: Fair allocation of credit between basic physiologists and the drug-development scientists, and treatment of Mojsov's contribution
The longlist does not name every historical contributor (for example Habener), which limits the configurations available
Long-term safety and neuropsychiatric effects of the drugs are still being characterized

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided genetically targeted, millisecond-precision control of defined cell types with light, and has become a foundational tool across neuroscience and beyond, enabling causal circuit dissection and early translational work such as vision restoration. Originality and methodological impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The discovery of channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and the demonstration of their use to control neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth, and others, with Miesenboeck's earlier photosensitization work) are separate contributions. Six names are credited and only three can be chosen. I would prefer Deisseroth for the neuronal implementation and broad development, with Nagel and Hegemann for the channel discovery; this leaves Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck out, which is a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The technique has been confirmed in thousands of independent studies for two decades; therapeutic application is still early, but as a tool its impact is established and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Intractable allocation among six credited people with a three-person limit
Whether the prize would be considered a technology prize rather than a discovery in physiology or medicine
Clinical translation is limited so far

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-based antisense correction of SMN2 splicing, culminating in nusinersen, converted spinal muscular atrophy from a fatal infantile disease into a treatable one. It is a clear, elegant demonstration of RNA-targeted therapy with dramatic clinical effect.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing regulatory elements and the ISS-N1 target concept with collaborators, and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and development at Ionis. Two laureates give a clean and fair configuration, though other contributors (for example Hua, Singh and clinical investigators) fall outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Long-term clinical data from several years of treatment and approvals around the world show durable benefit; the field has been strengthened by subsequent antisense and other RNA therapeutics. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Relative weighting of academic splicing mechanism versus pharmaceutical development
Contributions of other people not in the credited names
Whether the prize could be seen as better combined with a broader RNA-therapeutics concept

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and represent a new treatment modality, with a clear route from engineering concept to patient benefit and continuing expansion to autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain were responsible for the pivotal costimulatory-domain CAR designs and the first clinical successes in leukemia and lymphoma. Rosenberg is a major figure in adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells, but I regard the engineering of the CAR as the core discovery. Zelig Eshhar's original chimeric receptor work is not in the supplied credited names, and this is a real attribution gap.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products, long follow-up and independent confirmation in multiple centres; recognition is timely, though toxicity, solid-tumour limitations and secondary malignancy concerns are still being worked through.
uncertainties: Omission of Eshhar from the credited names
Rosenberg's relative contribution versus June and Sadelain
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and long-term safety

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identification and its link to narcolepsy opened the molecular understanding of sleep-wake regulation and has produced orexin-receptor antagonists for insomnia and agonists now in development. It is an excellent example of a gene-to-disease-to-drug path in neurology.
assessment.attribution: The 1998 identification of orexin and receptors by Sakurai and Yanagisawa, the parallel discovery of hypocretins by de Lecea and Kilduff, and Mignot's canine Hcrtr2 narcolepsy gene are all key. Five names are credited; Yanagisawa, Sakurai and Mignot give a balanced configuration but this leaves out the independent discovery by the de Lecea/Kilduff group, which would be disputed.
assessment.maturity: Replicated broadly: human narcolepsy type 1 involves orexin neuron loss, approved antagonists exist, and agonists are in trials. The interpretation is stable and the recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority dispute between the two groups naming the peptides
Allocation among five credited people
Orexin agonist therapies still in late clinical development

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR and the mTOR pathway as the central regulator of cell growth in response to nutrients and growth factors, with impact on cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression. It is an original, widely general mechanism of lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and its function in growth control, building on the rapamycin work. Sabatini contributed to the identification of mTOR and the mTORC1/2 regulatory machinery in mammalian cells. Schreiber's chemical-biology work on FKBP12-rapamycin is relevant but earlier and more about the ligand. Hall is the most decisive figure.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across species and decades; therapeutic payoff (rapalogs in transplant and oncology) is real but the broader hoped-for clinical use, including in ageing, is still not established. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Contributions of other mTOR pioneers (for example Heitman) are not in the credited names
Limited clinical impact of rapalogs outside narrow indications
Possible priority dispute with the rapamycin target-identification literature

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed and triggers interferon and inflammatory responses, connecting infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and ageing. It is a new innate-immunity paradigm with a clear molecular mechanism, including the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the DNA sensor and messenger, and Barber discovered STING as the essential adaptor. Ishikawa, Sun and Wu also contributed to STING and cGAS work, but a two-person prize is the cleanest.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is very well confirmed mechanistically, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) has so far been modest, so the medical impact is still emerging. Recognition is slightly early or at the edge of timely.
uncertainties: Limited clinical validation of STING-directed drugs
Overlapping contributions of other groups (for example Vance, Hornung, Ablasser) not in credited names
Allocation among five credited people

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus and thalamus transformed the management of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor and has spread to dystonia and other disorders. As a neurologist I know its clinical value well; it is a major, durable therapy.
assessment.attribution: Benabid's 1987 to 1993 demonstration of high-frequency thalamic and subthalamic stimulation is the decisive contribution, with Delong's basal ganglia circuit model and animal work by others as the scientific basis. Only Benabid is credited, so I propose him alone; Delong would be a natural partner but is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Decades of randomized trials and wide clinical use make it mature. It is more a clinical invention than a mechanistic discovery, and the mechanism of action remains incompletely understood.
uncertainties: Absence of Delong and others from the credited names
Fit as discovery versus clinical technique
Mechanism of action is not fully resolved
